Neither a universal loss-of-function mechanism nor simple haploinsufficiency explains all reported variants.

evidence.reference_title: A novel variant of CDK19 causes a severe neurodevelopmental disorder with infantile spasms.
evidence.snippet: We identified a novel de novo missense variant c.92C > A (p.Thr31Asn) in CDK19 that was classified as a likely pathogenic disease-causing variant.

nodes.description: Recurrent ATP-loop allele with increased activity in biochemical assays. It fails stringent fly rescue assays but restores selected functions under milder knockdown conditions; lifespan and myofibril defects can remain.

evidence.reference_title: Uncovering functional insights into human pathogenic variants in CDK19 using Drosophila models.
evidence.snippet: Y32H can functionally compensate for Cdk8 depletion in a manner similar to wild-type CDK19.

nodes.description: Recurrent ATP-loop substitution encoded by c.82G>C or c.82G>A in the 2021 cohort. Autophosphorylation and substrate phosphorylation are reduced.

evidence.reference_title: CDK19-related disorder results from both loss-of-function and gain-of-function de novo missense variants.
evidence.snippet: kinase activity of protein was lower for p.Gly28Arg and higher for p.Tyr32His substitutions compared with that of the wild-type protein.
